summary: Business Expansion Deferred Loan Program (BEDL) incentive for Allegany County

structured_extraction.program_description: A dedicated funding resource for small businesses that are ready to expand their footprint in Allegany County. The program seeks to help new companies become established in Allegany County or to help existing companies grow in order to expand employment opportunities, export capacity or placemaking.
structured_extraction.agency: Allegany County Economic and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible applicants can qualify for a low-interest loan from $10,000 to $50,000. Recipients have the opportunity to have up to half (50%) of the loan forgiven, based on predefined performance metrics such as job creation. Loans over $40,000 require a 1:1 match. Payments may be deferred for up to six months after the loan draw.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with less than 15 full-time employees that are ready to expand their footprint in Allegany County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible uses of funding include any costs that expand the productive capacity of the business that lead to long term, sustainable growth. This includes tangible assets such as equipment and furniture. Ineligible uses include staff costs, salaries, the acquisition or capital improvements of an existing building, or the construction of a new building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be physically present in Allegany County through the ownership or long-term commercial lease of a physical asset. Businesses operating out of personal residencies can also apply if they intend to expand to a commercial location.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit, tax-paying entity in good standing with Allegany County and the State of Maryland.
Must have less than fifteen (15) full-time employees.
Must clearly illustrate the ability to offer a tangible product or service.
Loans over $40,000 require a 1:1 match in funding.
A developed business plan approved by the local Small Business Development Center Representative is required.
Must provide proof of capacity through filed patents, existing sales figures, taxes paid, owned assets, or availability of capital/financing.
Projects that have already received funding from the Invest Allegany program are ineligible.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are by invitation only from a qualified member of Allegany County Economic and Community Development (ECD), after meeting pre-established criteria. Interested businesses should contact the ECD team to start a conversation. A review committee will make final recommendations to the Board of County Commissioners for approval.

summary: CleanTech Research & Development Grant Program incentive for Allegany County

structured_extraction.program_description: The CleanTech Research & Development Grant (CRD Grant) seeks to advance new innovations in environmental science and technology through subsidizing research and development costs to local firms associated with work that is contracted through the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science (UMCES) Appalachian Laboratory.
structured_extraction.agency: Allegany County Economic and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The grant will provide a 1:1 match for research costs, up to $50,000 per project, incurred from and paid directly to the Appalachian Lab. Awards will be capped at $50,000 per project and will fund half of the overall project cost. Projects that total more than $100,000 will not be subsidized more than the $50,000 maximum.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit, tax-paying entities based in Allegany County involved in environmental technology solutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible uses of funding include any and all costs incurred from the use of or research contracted through the Appalachian Lab and/or its staff, for the purposes of developing a new product or service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be physically present in Allegany County through the ownership or long-term commercial lease of a physical asset. Those businesses that are operating out of personal residencies can also apply, as long as it is clearly illustrated that they intend to eventually expand to a commercial location, as part of their narrative.
requirements_list: Applicants must be for-profit, tax-paying entities that are in good standing with Allegany County and the State of Maryland.
Applicants may only apply via a formal invitation from a qualified member of Allegany County Economic and Community Development or an indication from a staff member of the Appalachian Lab.
Business must clearly illustrate the ability to offer a tangible product or service.
Provide a 1:1 match for research costs.
A quote for research services or lab usage from the Appalachian Lab is required before consideration for approval.
A letter of approval from the Appalachian Lab, indicating the scientific value of the proposed research, is required.
Awardees must maintain a commercial presence in Allegany County for at least four (4) years after being awarded the grant or be required to reimburse the grant value.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should fill out a contact form. A member of the Allegany County Economic and Community Development team will reach out to discuss the research project and help facilitate contact with the Appalachian Lab. Applications are by invitation only. All applications will be reviewed by Allegany County. The Department of Economic and Community Development and the Appalachian Lab will make final recommendations and submit them to the County Commissioners for grant approval.

program_name: Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board
summary: Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board incentive for Allegany County

structured_extraction.program_name: Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board
structured_extraction.program_description: A program created to catalyze economic development in Western Maryland by funding projects that make a substantial economic impact, bring significant employment opportunities, and/or increase the tax base in the region.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Assistance is offered as grants or loans for capital infrastructure and business development projects. The minimum award amount is $150,000, though smaller projects may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Matching funds are required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and organizations undertaking capital infrastructure or business development projects in Western Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for two categories: 1) Infrastructure Funding for projects such as broadband connectivity, road access improvement, utility connections, property purchases, and building/housing construction and improvements. 2) Business Development Funding for projects that create new jobs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program serves projects located in Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties.
requirements_list: Projects must create new jobs that pay at least 120% of the State Minimum Wage.
Infrastructure projects require a minimum 20% match of total project costs.
Business development projects require a minimum 10% match of total project costs.
Higher matching funds are given preference.
Projects must demonstrate significant job creation or provide significant increases to the taxable base.
The minimum grant amount is $150,000, with exceptions considered on a case-by-case basis.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The first round of applications has closed. Under a new process adopted in January 2024, inquiries should be made to the Executive Director, a Member of the Board, or the Economic Development Director in the county where the project will take place.

summary: Arundel Community Reinvestment (ACR) Fund incentive for Anne Arundel County

structured_extraction.program_description: The Arundel Community Reinvestment (ACR) Fund is designed to spur economic activity, investment, and improvement in specific designated areas within Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The ACR offers loans up to $100,000 to be repaid over three to seven years at zero percent interest. In addition to financial assistance, the program includes professional architectural services. ACR Fund loan recipients will also be offered a companion loan of up to $500,000 through AAEDC’s VOLT Fund.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners or business owners with a lease.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible improvements including renovation and upgrades to building exteriors and site improvements, including landscaping. The companion loan may be used to finance additional improvements including tenant improvements, the purchase of equipment, and working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The fund is available in Anne Arundel County’s eleven Commercial Revitalization Districts; parts of the City of Annapolis; Anne Arundel County’s Enterprise zone, located in Brooklyn Park; and designated commercial corridors located in South County.
requirements_list: Loans are limited to 90% of total project costs.
Applicant must be a property owner or a business owner with a lease.
Property must be located in an eligible area.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals are asked to contact AAEDC to discuss the process and verify that the particular property is eligible. An online application is available.

summary: Community Revitalization Tax Credit incentive for Anne Arundel County

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for property owners undertaking renovation/rehabilitation, new construction, or demolition and redevelopment of a building site. The property must be commercially or industrially zoned and located in one of the County’s 11 designated Commercial Revitalization districts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a property tax credit for up to five years equal to the incremental increase in real property tax assessment for improvements of at least $100,000 of assessed value.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Property owners have 120 days following the issuance of the notice of assessment by the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation to apply for the credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners undertaking renovation/rehabilitation of an existing building or new construction or demolition and redevelopment of their building site.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit supports improvements including renovation/rehabilitation of an existing building, new construction, or demolition and redevelopment of a building site.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The commercially or industrially zoned property must be located in one of Anne Arundel County’s 11 designated Commercial Revitalization districts.
requirements_list: Improvements must total at least $100,000 of assessed value.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners must apply for the credit within 120 days following the issuance of the notice of assessment by the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation.

summary: Grocery Store Tax Credit incentive for Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_name: Grocery Store Personal Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers a personal property tax credit to grocery stores that are locating or making significant renovations within targeted areas in Baltimore City. The program aims to address the lack of access to healthy food choices and serve as a catalyst for increased economic development in the community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10-year, 80 percent credit against personal property tax for supermarkets locating in or making significant improvements in targeted areas. The personal property typically covers furniture, fixtures and equipment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Initial application must be received by October 1. Continuing eligibility forms must be submitted by November 30 each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Grocery stores or supermarkets locating or renovating in designated incentive areas within Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The property must be located in a designated grocery store incentive area within Baltimore City. Applicants can determine if a location is eligible by using the CityView website.
requirements_list: For newly constructed stores, must have expended on new personal property an amount equal to or greater than $150,000 or $25 per square foot.

For newly renovated stores, must have expended on new personal property an amount based on total floor space: at least $5/sq ft for stores <= 20,000 sq ft; at least $8/sq ft for stores > 20,000 and <= 45,000 sq ft; and at least $10/sq ft for stores > 45,000 sq ft.
Must have at least 500 square feet dedicated to the sale of fruits and vegetables.
Must have at least 500 square feet dedicated to the sale of other perishable goods including meat, seafood and dairy products.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must first pre-qualify for the credit based on the location. After pre-qualification is granted and the construction or renovation is complete, the applicant must submit an initial application form to request verification of the tax credit qualifications. Once a tax credit is granted, an annual qualification form is required for the ten-year period of the credit.

summary: Foreign Trade Zone incentive for Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_description: A foreign-trade zone is a federally designated area within the U.S. but considered outside U.S. Customs territory for assessing import duties and taxes. The Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC) administers Foreign Trade Zone #74, which provides economic incentives to companies importing or exporting international goods. It allows a company to conduct activities on U.S. soil that would otherwise be more cost-effective abroad, enhancing performance through cost-saving and operational benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Foreign Trade Zone procedures can enhance a company’s performance through several cost-saving and operational benefits, including deferred duties, reduced processing fees, and streamlined logistics.
structured_extraction.program_audience: A wide variety of businesses, including companies importing or exporting international goods for their warehouse, distribution, and manufacturing facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Foreign Trade Zone #74’s service area consists of almost 1,000 total acres of designated industrial and distribution space in the listed counties. Under the Alternative Site Framework (ASF), a company can be located at any property in the designated service area.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A company can quickly complete the activation process within a few weeks. To learn more about FTZ #74 and its benefits, please contact the FTZ Director.

summary: Facade Improvement Grant (FIG) incentive for Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_description: A city-wide program that provides matching grants to make exterior improvements to commercial and industrial properties. These grants are to assist businesses and property owners fund building improvements that noticeably improve the look and feel of the surrounding commercial area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Offers matching grants for commercial properties, vacant and corner commercial properties, industrial properties, and shopping centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and property owners of commercial and industrial properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior improvements to commercial and industrial properties, including building façades, storefronts, signs, awnings, outdoor seating areas, and other outdoor improvements.
requirements_list: Work cannot begin until the grant is awarded and an agreement letter is signed and returned to BDC.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, please use the application form available on the program website. For more information, review the FIG fact sheet and application. If you have questions, please contact info@BaltimoreDevelopment.com.

program_name: Neighbohood Impact Investment Fund (NIIF) Direct Loans
summary: Neighbohood Impact Investment Fund (NIIF) Direct Loans incentive for Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_name: Neighbohood Impact Investment Fund (NIIF) Direct Loans
structured_extraction.program_description: NIIF provides direct loans for impactful development projects that can be accessed at any point in the development timeline, including acquisition, predevelopment, construction, and term financing. NIIF also provides bridge financing to accelerate grants or other future funding sources and subordinate loans to complement other lenders. NIIF financing is used for housing, commercial development, community facilities, and mixed-use projects.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides various types of direct loans for development projects: Term Loans, Bridge Loans, Construction Loans, Acquisition Loans, and Predevelopment Loans. Loan amounts are up to $3,000,000 for most types ($100,000 for predevelopment loans, higher amounts possible with collateral). Interest rates start from 5.0%, subject to underwriting. Terms vary by loan type (e.g., up to 7 years for Term Loans). Fees typically include a $5,000 commitment fee, an origination fee up to 1.50%, and third-party fees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Real estate developers, Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs), and other intermediaries involved in larger scale real estate related development or acquisition projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for acquisition, predevelopment, construction, and term financing for housing, commercial development, community facilities, and mixed-use projects. Specific uses include the purchase of land and buildings, hard and soft costs for construction or renovation, and early-stage project costs like engineering, design, and environmental studies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Investment is restricted to specific Eligible Neighborhoods within Baltimore City. An interactive map of these neighborhoods is available on the NIIF website.
requirements_list: Loan to value (LTV) limits apply, generally up to 90-95%; non-profit sponsors may be eligible for higher LTV.
Collateral/security is required for most loans, which may include liens on real estate or pledges on grant receivables.
Bridge loans require an identified take-out source, such as tax credit equity, grants, or permanent financing.
Predevelopment loans over $100,000 require a pledge of collateral, strength of the guarantor, or other underwritten repayment sources.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must first confirm the project is in an eligible Baltimore City neighborhood using the online map, determine which financing option is needed, and then complete and submit the online intake form.

summary: Outdoor Spaces Grant incentive for Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant to assist business owners with the cost of installing outdoor seating, parklets, landscaping, and other features that enhance a business’ use of outdoor space, encourage community interactions, and promote a vibrant street life for Baltimore neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $5,000 in matching funds reimbursement for qualified expenses. Grant funds are reimbursed to the applicant following proof of completion and payment for the entire project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business owners in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible uses include: café tables and chairs, benches, curbside facilities (parklets, patios), shade structures, outdoor lighting, pots, planters, planter boxes, trellises, plants and landscaping, mobile vending structures, and architectural/design services (up to 25% of total project cost).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible locations include: Public Right of Way (sidewalk or parking spaces adjacent to a business), outdoor seating areas/courtyards on private property, and community spaces on public or private property for the use of the general public.
requirements_list: Requires matching funds.
Work must not begin prior to grant approval.
Construction must be completed within 120 days of award letter.
Applicants must obtain two quotes from licensed contractors for installations performed by a 3rd party (one quote required for retail products).
Cost of plants and landscaping is limited to 25% of the total amount of the grant.
Applicant must agree to maintain all improvements for a period of three years.
For work in the public right of way, a valid Curbside Commercial Permit and/or related Minor Privilege Permits are required.
Applicants/businesses must be in good legal standing with Federal, State or local authorities.
Installations on private property must be for the use of the general public.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants e-mail or mail a completed application package which includes the application form, W-9, sketch/rendering of improvements, cost estimates, and applicable permits or MOUs. A BDC staff person assists throughout the process. To receive reimbursement, grantees must submit a Reimbursement Request Form, photos of the completed work, and copies of all payments.

program_name: Francis Scott Key Bridge Business Assistance
summary: Francis Scott Key Bridge Business Assistance incentive for Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_name: Francis Scott Key Bridge Business Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: A collection of resources and financial assistance programs for businesses impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse. The assistance includes loans, grants, wage subsidies, and tax payment waivers to help businesses address temporary revenue loss, retain employees, and manage operating expenses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple programs are available, including: 1) Small Business Administration (SBA) Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDLs) up to $2 million. 2) Maryland Department of Commerce's Port of Baltimore Emergency Assistance Program offering grants up to $100,000. 3) Maryland Department of Housing & Community Development (DHCD) Neighborhood BusinessWorks Program providing grants up to $50,000 and loans up to $500,000. 4) Baltimore City’s Wage Subsidy Program of up to $7,500 per worker. 5) Comptroller of Maryland offering waivers on certain business taxes and IFTA requirements. Note: The Maryland Department of Labor’s Port of Baltimore Worker Retention Program is no longer accepting applications.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by specific assistance program. Some programs have ended, while others are still accepting applications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses of all sizes, including some private, non-profit organizations, that have been financially impacted by the Key Bridge collapse and the resulting disruption to the Port of Baltimore.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for normal operating expenses, including fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, other bills, and employee retention.
requirements_list: Must be a business impacted by the Key Bridge collapse.
Must demonstrate economic and financial injury, such as a reduction in business revenue or increased costs.
Some sub-programs are specific to Baltimore City-based businesses.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses are encouraged to complete the Business Impact Survey. To apply for specific assistance, businesses must follow the links provided on the main webpage for each program, which lead to separate application pages on the websites of the administering agencies (e.g., SBA, Maryland Department of Commerce, DHCD).

program_name: Buy Into Bmore Fixed Pricing Program
summary: Buy Into Bmore Fixed Pricing Program incentive for Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_name: Buy Into Bmore Fixed Pricing Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A sales program for specific City-owned vacant buildings and lots in Baltimore City. The program aims to streamline the disposition process and offers a clearly defined, fixed pricing structure for various purchaser types, including homeowners, developers, and non-profits, to encourage the rehabilitation of vacant properties.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This is a fixed-price sales program for city-owned properties. Prices vary by purchaser and property type. For vacant buildings: $1 for homeowners and Community Land Trusts, $1,000 for non-profits (<=50 employees), and $3,000 for for-profit developers and larger non-profits (>50 employees). For vacant lots: $1 for homeowners and Community Land Trusts, $500 for non-profits (<=50 employees), and $1,000 for for-profit developers and larger non-profits (>50 employees).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Future homeowners (prioritizing current Baltimore City residents), community land trusts, non-profit developers, and for-profit developers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program is for the purchase and rehabilitation of vacant city-owned buildings and lots. Properties must be developed for residential or mixed-use that includes a residential component. Vacant lots may also be used for green space or as a side yard for an adjacent primary residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This program applies to properties that fall within the E-J Housing Market Typology in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Applicants must have an available rehabilitation budget of at least $90,000 per property.
A use and occupancy permit must be obtained within 12 months from the date of settlement.
Homeowners must maintain the property as their primary residence for a minimum of 5 years after issuance of the use and occupancy permit.
Applicants are subject to a vetting process that checks for ownership of other vacant properties, legal impediments, and federal or state liens or judgments.
A $100 application fee is required, which is credited at settlement if approved or refunded if rejected.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. There is a homeowner priority application period. DHCD reviews applications and renders a decision within two weeks. If multiple qualified applications are received for the same property, they are reviewed in order of submission. The program aims for a 90-day processing timeline.

summary: Grant for Revitalizing Office Workspaces (GROW) incentive for Baltimore County

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time grant award to eligible businesses signing their first commercial lease in Baltimore County to help offset initial leasing expenses.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Economic and Workforce Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A one-time grant award of $8 per square foot, up to a maximum of $80,000 per business, is available to help offset initial leasing expenses. All awards are subject to the availability of funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible businesses signing their first commercial lease in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To help offset initial leasing expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible properties include Class A and Class B Office space. Class A and Class B Flex space will be considered for businesses with a demonstrated need for laboratory space.
requirements_list: Must be the business's first commercial lease in Baltimore County.
Business must execute a direct lease with a landlord for a minimum 36-month term.
Leased property must be for a minimum of 500 square feet.
Program application must be received within 180 days of lease execution.
Lease must be signed after February 14, 2025.
Applicants must have a minimum personal credit score of 625.
Retail, restaurant, independent financial, or insurance agent or broker establishments are not eligible.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Those interested in applying should submit a Program and Tax Credit Interest form online. The Business Services team will reach out to those who are eligible.

summary: Advanced Technology Loan Fund incentive for Baltimore County

structured_extraction.program_audience: Technology based businesses and businesses acquiring technology equipment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used to finance the acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion.

summary: Boost Loan Fund Program incentive for Baltimore County

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Start-up funding, Gap funding, Building improvements, Equipment acquisition, Lease improvements, Business acquisition, Work capital, Commercial real estate acquisition
requirements_list: Be classified as a small business by SBA Standards.
Have a personal credit score of 625 or higher.
Provide collateral as security for all loans.
Provide personal guarantees.

Some minor interior and equipment improvements may also be financed.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Economic and Workforce Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to a $60,000 interest-free loan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in one of 24 Commercial Revitalization Districts in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior improvements such as awnings, landscaping and signage. Some minor interior and equipment improvements may also be financed.

The Business Services team will reach out to those who are eligible. You can also contact businesshelp@baltimorecountymd.gov to get more information and download an application.

summary: Business Growth Loans incentive for Baltimore County

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maximum loan amount is $250,000. These are direct loans or loan guarantees.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To finance the acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For those interested in applying for a County finance program or tax credit, complete online form at https://www.baltimorecountymd.gov/departments/economic-and-workforce-development/business/financing-and-tax-credits, selecting the finance program or tax credit you are interested in. Our Business Services team will reach out to those who are eligible.

summary: Enterprise Zone (EZ) Tax Credit incentive for Baltimore County

structured_extraction.program_description: The purpose of the Enterprise Zone (EZ) Tax Credit is to insure retention and spur expansions of existing companies, promote development and occupancy of vacant, underutilized land and buildings, encourage the creation of well-paying new jobs, and support the revitalization of older office and industrial areas of Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying companies can benefit from property tax credits and income tax credits. The Real Property Tax Credit is available for companies that make improvements to real property, lasting for 10 years. For the first five years, the credit is 80% of the increased property tax from the investment, declining by 10% annually for the remaining five years. The State Income Tax Credit provides a one-time credit of up to $1,000 per new, full-time employee. This credit can increase up to $3,000 for a new employee meeting 'disadvantaged' criteria, with potential additional credits in the second and third years. Additionally, a BGE 'Rider 7' electricity price reduction program is available for companies meeting certain electricity load and employment increase thresholds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The Application should be submitted no later than December 31 to receive a property tax credit on the next July 1 tax bill.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses that make a new investment in real property or hire new employees within one of Baltimore County's three designated Enterprise Zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credits are based on capital investment in real property or the creation of new full-time jobs within the Enterprise Zone.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The incentive is available within three designated Enterprise Zones in Baltimore County: the Chesapeake Zone, the Southwest Enterprise Zone, and the Federal Center at Woodlawn.
requirements_list: Must make a new investment in real property in the Enterprise Zone or hire new employees that work inside the Zone.
Retail establishments are generally not eligible.
For the BGE 'Rider 7' program, companies must have new or incremental electricity load increases of 200kW or more per month and increase employment by at least 10 full-time equivalent persons.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, a company must complete and return an application to the Baltimore County Department of Economic Development. For the property tax credit, no further paperwork is needed. For income tax credits, Maryland Tax Form 500CR must be submitted with the annual tax return. Certification from the Maryland Department of Labor is required for the higher income tax credit for hiring 'economically disadvantaged' employees.

summary: Tax Exempt Bonds incentive for Baltimore County

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bond financing is available from $2.5 million to a maximum of $10 million.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Manufacturers and 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations

structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description:
The program provides a credit against Washington County's real property tax imposed on the increased assessed value of newly constructed or expanded premises. The credit amount and duration depend on the tier qualified for:
- TIER ONE: 52% for years 1-2; 39% for years 3-4; 26% for years 5-6.
- TIER TWO: 30% for years 1-2; 20% for years 3-4; 10% for years 5-6.
- TIER THREE: 100% for years 1-5; 75% for years 6-10; 50% for years 11-15.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New or established businesses that are either expanding or locating in Washington County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The property must be located in Washington County. For Tier One and Tier Two, the property must be within a Priority Funding Area. Business entities locating or expanding within an Enterprise Zone are not eligible to participate in this program.
requirements_list: A business must provide written notification of its intent to claim the tax credit and a completed application to the Washington County Department of Business Development before obtaining the premises or hiring employees.

TIER ONE (Existing Business): Must obtain at least 1,500 sq. ft. of new or expanded premises and employ at least 1 new permanent full-time position paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage within a 12-month period.

TIER TWO (New Business): Must obtain at least 2,500 sq. ft. of new or expanded premises and employ at least 5 new permanent full-time positions paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage within a 24-month period.
TIER THREE (New or Existing Business): Must invest at least $10,000,000 in capital improvements and create 100 new permanent full-time positions.

For Tiers One and Two, the premises must be a retail facility less than 3,000 sq. ft, a restaurant less than 2,500 sq. ft, a warehouse facility less than 30,000 sq. ft, or a distribution facility less than 30,000 sq. ft.
The business must continue to occupy the new or expanded premises and maintain the new permanent full-time positions for the duration of the tax credit period.

summary: High Performance Commercial Building Tax Incentive Program incentive for Washington County

structured_extraction.program_name: High Performance Commercial Building Tax Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for building owners in Washington County for the construction, renovation, or remodeling of commercial property that attains and maintains a LEED Certification level of Silver, Gold or Platinum. The tax credit is based on the increase in the property's assessed value resulting from the improvements.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The tax credit is applied against the increase in the assessed value of a property resulting from new construction or renovation. The credit amount is 20% of the increase for LEED Silver, 25% for LEED Gold, and 30% for LEED Platinum. The tax credit is applied for three consecutive years and may not be carried over to another tax year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: A taxpayer must apply for the tax credit within 1 (one) year after the building is certified as a 'high performance building'.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial buildings in Washington County.
requirements_list: The building must be a commercial property that has been newly constructed or renovated.
The building must achieve a silver, gold, or platinum rating from the United States Green Building Council (USGBC) under LEED-CS, LEED-EB, or LEED-NC systems.
The property owner must provide evidence of receipt of a use and occupancy certificate.
The property owner must provide certification of the LEED status.
To continue receiving the credit, the building owner must submit an annual letter of compliance attesting that all conditions of the original certification remain in place.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, the building owner must submit a completed and signed application along with a true and correct copy of the initial LEED certification request to the Washington County Department of Business Development. To receive the tax credit after approval, the applicant must submit a copy of the final USGBC project certification for the building.
